captions.text: This is the front door. Someone wanted good for you.
Tap I have an access code if a mosque gave you one.
The code may already be filled in. Type your name.
Type an email you can open later.
Pick a password you will remember.
Tap Join. That is enough to come in.
The short film sits at the top. The words being said sit underneath.
Pull the More tab up. Like, Save and Ready for more? sit under the words.
Tap the heart to keep this clip.
Tap Ready for more? when you want the longer cut.
A few short scenes help pick your first talk. There is no right answer.
Tap Let’s play.
Tap the picture that feels closest. You can skip a scene you would rather not sit with.
Someone in your circle opened HEARTS for you.
Tap Begin when you are ready.
A short welcome film may play here. You can watch it, or move on.
Tap Continue when you are ready for the next step.
A few short questions help pick a gentle first talk.
Tap the answer that fits. There is no wrong one.
Tap Find my first talk when you have answered.
This is a first talk picked from what you said.
Tap to start it, or go to your clips if you would rather watch something short first.
Each lane is one theme. Walk one subject at a time.
Tap a lane to watch its clips.
This is one teacher and the talks they gave.
Tap a talk to start it, or watch a short clip first.
This is the whole course: every talk, the count, and the time. Questions stay inside each talk.
Tap Start to open the first talk.
Type the email you joined with.
Type your password. The dots hide it.
Tap Sign in. Home opens when it matches.
Home is where you come back. A note from your mosque sits at the top when there is one.
Tap Watch today’s clips for a short film.
The film sits at the top. Questions stay quiet until you reach them, or tap a dot on the line.
Tap a dot to jump to a question. The talk pauses so you can write.
Type a sample answer in your own words.
If something someone else wrote does not sit right, tap the report mark and say so.
The garden is a quiet picture of time you have given. It is not a score.
Tap Keep this to write one small thing you did today.
Type a sample line. Only you see it.
Tap Keep this again to save it.
These are plain counts of time you have given: talks, answers, seats and lines. Nothing here is a score.
These doors come from the hadith of Jibril. A door lights when you finish a talk placed in it.
Tap a door to read it.
Read the door, then look at the talks that sit here.
Tap I’ve read this on a seat when you have sat with it.
These are seats from al-Ghunya, grouped by door.
Tap a door to see its seats.
Answers you write in a talk are kept here, whether you share them or not. A teacher’s reply sits under the ones you offered.
Lines you kept from talks sit here: verses, hadith and short sayings.
Tap By speaker to group them another way.
Open one line to read it again.
This is your name, your week, your saved clips and your settings.
Open the name row.
Type the name you want on this phone.
Tap Save name.
Each switch saves as you flip it. Sound, privacy and the account sit in their own groups.
Flip one switch. It saves on its own.
Nights are the evenings you can come to in person. The board is a note for everyone in your circle.
Type a short note for the board.
Tap Post.
Clips you kept sit here. Open one to watch it again. Nothing here is a test.
These lines come from time you have actually given, not from a label. If a row has no reason yet, you have not sat with that theme this week.
Five short questions, in different words from last time. There is no right answer.
Tap the line that fits. The next question comes up on its own.
These are people you can call or visit if you need support now. The numbers are for this mosque. Back to HEARTS returns you to the opening.
Write to the team here. You do not need an email.
Tap Send. They will read it.
Missions you joined, and what the group decided, sit here. You cannot change a decision from this list.
These are meetings at your mosque or school. Say if you are coming.
Tap Suggest a gathering if you want to propose one.
Type a name for the evening.
Type when it is, as day, month, year, then the time.
Tap Send it to the desk. This does not book the room on its own.
A short note after the gathering. Only you and the team see it unless you share.
Type one thing you will carry.
Tap Send. You can still change the words later.
This is the front door of the desk. The counts are who has joined and how busy the last two weeks have been.
Tap Copy to put the join link on your clipboard.
Each row is a learner. Hide test accounts stays on so practice logins do not clutter the list.
Choose a course for the first learner. The Give button stays still until you do.
Tap Give. Confirm it, and they see the course on Lanes next time they open the app.
Only answers a learner chose to share appear here. Private ones are counted and never shown.
Tick Anonymise to turn names into Learner A, Learner B, and so on.
Open the download box when you need a file. The download is written down.
Compass is a gentle monthly look. Learners never see a number. You see the scales.
Open one learner to see why a talk was put forward.
This is one learner over the months. They still only see a gentle line, never these numbers.
A study plan spreads one course across the days you tick. Parts stay in order.
Tick a day the plan should use. Leave a day unticked and nothing is placed on it.
Earned means they watched a part this week. Held means you welcome them in at the door.
Tick Let them in anyway when you are letting someone in without a ticket.
Publish a date, share the link, and take the register from Attendance.
Open Attendance when you need the list of who came.
This is the register. Who said they would come, who arrived, and a download when you need a list. It does not change who is invited.
This is where the team looks at concerns, and at words the screen held back. A gold box at the top is for the named person when someone may need support today.
The same care list, across every mosque. Hide or keep an item, and send a short note.
Write a short note. It appears on Home until they dismiss it.
Tap Share this note.
Write a short note for one mosque. Learners see it on Home.
Tap Share this note.
Search looks at subject titles.
Or type a new subject of your own. It belongs to this mosque.
Tap Save subject when the name is right. Questions are added in the editor.
This is one subject: its topics, films, and the questions that pause them.
Paste a YouTube link to add a film. A new film is a draft until you publish it.
The library is the shared catalogue. Link a course so learners can open it.
Open a pack to see the courses inside. Adding one keeps it in step with the shared library.
A code says who someone is and which courses they see. Send the link so nobody has to type the letters.
Tap Copy on a code. WhatsApp and the QR use the same address.
These are the questions a newcomer sees before the clips. You can keep them, change the words, or leave a scene out.
The help contacts on this page are what the help screen shows.
Joining questions are asked once. Each answer points to a door. The door with the most answers chooses the first course.
Paste a YouTube link. A line may end with a bar and a speaker name.
Type a name if you are making a new course. Nothing is saved until you bring the ticked rows in.
Look up reads the list before anything is saved.

master-bring-in.title: Bring in on the master desk

captions.text: Paste one link, a playlist, or a channel.
Pick the caption language. English is the usual choice.
Look up shows the length and whether captions are listed. Nothing is saved yet.
The sheet is a workbook you can download, edit, and upload again. Preview first. Nothing is saved until you apply.
Tap the blank template. An empty export of real courses is refused, so the blank one is the safe download.
Scope says what the workbook covers: the whole library, one mosque, or one course.
Download the blank template, edit it, then upload it and preview before anything is saved.
Search for talks on a topic. Nothing goes live until you apply the preview on the sheet page.
Type what the sheet should be about.

master-creator.title: Sheet creator on the master desk

captions.text: Name a topic and the desk drafts a workbook. You still preview and apply it before learners see anything.
Upload the timed transcript a sheet points at. Each file gets a number you can paste back into the sheet. You do not need the raw data console.
Circle answers are light examples so a question is never empty. They are never counted as progress.
Open a talk to draft or edit its examples.

master-circle.title: Circle answers on the master desk

captions.text: The same circle answers, for the shared library.
Open a talk.
Each step is one job after a talk is brought in. A run uses that mosque’s own AI account when one is connected. Otherwise the built-in drafts are used.
Open a step to read its prompt.
The prompt is the instruction. Saving writes a new version. The live one stays until you mark this one live. Try it on a single talk first.
Change the name people see, then save before you leave.
The time zone is the city of the mosque. It does not change the clocks on people’s phones.
A test shows some learners one wording and others another, then counts what they do. Learners are never told. A teacher’s words are never tested.
The kill switch stops every running test at once. Everyone sees the usual words again.
Insights is a look at how people move through HEARTS. Taps and clip watches stay as counts. Typed text and answers are never stored.
The calendar knows Friday, Ramadan, the two Eids, and seasons you add. The Islamic day moves on at sunset. A suggested line never reaches a learner until you approve it.
A mission is a warm ask, never a scolding.
Open one, or start a new ask.
Each portal is one mosque, with its own admin, codes and people.
Open the studio when you want to choose courses and features.
Type the name people will see.
Type a short address. It becomes the link.
Tap Next for courses, then features. Do not open it until you mean to.
Features decide what this mosque shows. Saving takes effect at once.
Tap Start small for videos, questions and the Garden only.
Tap Everything if you want every switch on. Leave the page without saving if you were only looking.
The shared courses every mosque can link. Changes you make here show up for them straight away.
Open a course to edit it.
This is one shared subject. Mosques link it. They do not get their own copy.
A pack is the set of courses a code opens. Tick the box only when you want people who already hold the pack to receive a new course too.
The tick adds newly ticked courses to learners who keep a saved course list. Leave it unticked and they keep the list they joined with.
Plans learners and teachers have shared out across the days. It is a guide. People can still watch at their own pace.
Nights and gatherings across the mosques. Open a portal desk to take the register.
The scenes a newcomer meets before the clips. Publishing checks the rules: enough options, no blocked words, and one crisis option.
Lanes are the themes the opening uses to pick clips. The titles here are what learners see. Change one with care.
Walk the opening as a newcomer would, without making an account. Nothing here is saved against a real person.
Pick a tap for a scene and see what the phone would work out.
Scales and bands are the Compass language. Learners never see these names, only a gentle line. Change them with care.
Asked once when someone joins, so the first talk is a gentle place to start. The default set is already on every mosque.
Counts across mosques that opted in. A trend only appears when enough people are in the group. A name is never shown.
Machine drafts wait here for a person. Approve what reads true. Send back what does not.
Tap Approve when a row is ready for learners.
Questions that pause a film wait here. Approve what reads true. Approved work is what learners see.
Answers the safety screen hid wait here. Show the ones that are fine. Keep the rest hidden.
Tap Show in the swarm when an answer is fine for other learners to see.
Tiers are the short, medium and longer ways into the same talk. Learners only see checked work.
Open one to check the times and the lines.
Check the times and the lines before you mark a talk as checked.
Pick a course. The talks stay in order.
Tick the days that suit you. Leave a day unticked and nothing lands on it.
Tap the button to put the talks on your week. It is a guide. You can still watch at your own pace.
Say if you are coming, maybe, or cannot this time.
Tap I’m coming.
Three short steps. First, a line of welcome.
Tap Next. You can run this again from Settings. Nothing here deletes what you already made.
A short clip is playing. The longer cut is under More.
Pull the More tab up.
Tap Ready for more?. This is the longer cut of the same talk.
Tap Back when you want the short clips again.
This is where a live session starts for the people in this portal.
Give the session a name people will recognise.
Paste a YouTube or Vimeo link if that is where you are streaming.
Every portal’s live sessions sit here. Open a portal desk to start or end one.
Open a portal desk when you need to go live for that mosque.
Each row is a clip. The coloured words are how the director framed it on the phone.
Open a clip when you want to change one segment.
Play the crop, then change a segment when the pick is wrong. The film stays where it is.
Live recordings are the video sessions for your portal.
When one is on you can watch and send a question. A replay sits here afterwards if your teacher kept one.

skipped.default: Fallback sentences for a screen with no page of its own. There is no task to film.
skipped.closed: Shown only when a portal is paused. The seeded demo stays open so the other pages can be filmed.
skipped.feature-unavailable: Shown only when a feature is switched off. The seeded demo has every feature on.
skipped.mission-page: The seeded demo has no A mission screen to open.
skipped.mission-missing: The seeded demo has no A mission screen to open.
skipped.live-screen: The seeded demo has no A live talk screen to open.
skipped.gather-door: The seeded demo has no At the door screen to open.
